title: Account Age, Returned Payments and the Commercial Credit Account Room Tolerance
content:
In a room payment on a Commercial Credit Account, the age of the account and its returned payments decide how much of the tier's over-limit tolerance percentage enters **the tolerance percentage used**.

### Clause

The share of the tier's over-limit tolerance percentage that enters the tolerance percentage used is nothing for an account opened less than ten whole years before today that carries a returned payment entry dated less than the tier's returned-payment lookback in whole months before today, one half for an account that meets exactly one of those two conditions, and the whole percentage for an account that meets neither.

Whole months between a date and today are the difference in calendar months, less one when today's day of the month is earlier than that date's day of the month, with no move of a month-end date to a shorter month's last day. Ten whole years are 120 whole months; the account's age runs from its opened date. The returned-payment lookback is 12 months on every tier.

### Condition table

| Opened fewer than 120 whole months before today | Returned payment entry dated less than the lookback before today | Share of the tier's over-limit tolerance percentage |
|---|---|---|
| yes | yes | nothing |
| yes | no | one half (50 percent) |
| no | yes | one half (50 percent) |
| no | no | the whole (100 percent) |

### Cases (hypothetical, today 10 April)

- Opened 10 April ten years earlier (120 whole months), no returned payment in the lookback: the whole percentage.
- Opened 11 April ten years earlier (119 whole months), a returned payment dated 11 April of the previous year (11 whole months): nothing.
- On a 10 percent tier, a share of 50 percent puts 5 percentage points of the tier's tolerance into the tolerance percentage used.
